arxiv-2101-00174.title: Chaos in QCD? Gap equations and their fractal properties.
arxiv-2101-00174.creator: Thomas Klähn, Lee C. Loveridge, Mateusz Cierniak
arxiv-2101-00174.description: Abstract We discuss how iterative solutions of QCD inspired gap-equations at finite chemical potential show domains of chaotic behavior as well as non-chaotic domains which represent one or the other of the only two - usually distinct - positive mass gap solutions with broken or restored chiral symmetry, respectively.

arxiv-2202-01753.description: Abstract The task of multi-dimensional numerical integration is frequently encountered in physics and other scientific fields, e.g., in modeling the effects of systematic uncertainties in physical systems and in Bayesian parameter estimation. Multi-dimensional integration is often time-prohibitive on CPUs. Efficient implementation on many-core architectures is challenging as the workload across the integration space cannot be predicted a priori.

arxiv-2509-26633.description: Abstract A dominant paradigm for teaching humanoid robots complex skills is to retarget human motions as kinematic references to train reinforcement learning (RL) policies. However, existing retargeting pipelines often struggle with the significant embodiment gap between humans and robots, producing physically implausible artifacts like foot-skating and penetration.

britannica-1911-rivoli-veronese.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-rivoli-veronese.description: Article 'Rivoli Veronese' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 23), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. province of Verona, on a hill on the right; bank of the Adige, 13 m. It is celebrated as the scene of the battle in which, on the 15th of January 1797, Napoleon inflicted a decisive defeat upon the Austrians commanded by Josef Alvintzi, Baron von Barberek (1735–1810) (see French Revolutionary Wars).

pmc-11284205.title: Novel nano composites from Citrus limon and Citrullus colocynthis agricultural wastes for biomedical applications
pmc-11284205.creator: Nagwa A Kamel, D A Wissa, Salwa L Abd-El-Messieh
pmc-11284205.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In recent years, academic and industrial research has focused on using agro-waste for energy and new material production to promote sustainable development and lessen environmental issues. In this study, new nanocomposites based on polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)-Starch using two affordable agricultural wastes, Citrus limon peels (LP) and Citrullus colocynthis (Cc) shells and seeds powders with different concentrations (2, 5, 10, and 15 wt%) as bio-fillers were prepared.

pmc-11587678.title: Designer immune cells
pmc-11587678.creator: Naoki Hosen
pmc-11587678.description: at has demonstrated that “cell” modalities can be established as a revolutionary treatment modality. The cell types used for designer immune cells are not only T cells. NK cells, macrophages, or iPS-derived immune cells are now being tested as sources of designer immune cells.

pmc-11677791.title: Role of the Foliar Endophyte Colletotrichum in the Resistance of Invasive Ageratina adenophora to Disease and Abiotic Stress
pmc-11677791.creator: Ailing Yang, Yuxuan Li, Zhaoying Zeng, Hanbo Zhang, Gary A Strobel
pmc-11677791.description: Plant-associated fungi often drive plant invasion success by increasing host growth, disease resistance, and tolerance to environmental stress. A high abundance of Colletotrichum asymptomatically accumulated in the leaves of Ageratina adenophora. In this study, we aimed to clarify whether three genetically distinct endophytic Colletotrichum isolates (AX39, AX115, and AX198) activate invasive plant defenses against disease and environmental stress.

pmc-12563640.title: Genetic Alteration Profiling in North Macedonian Lung Cancer Patients
pmc-12563640.creator: Aleksandar Eftimov, Rubens Jovanovic, Slavica Kostadinova Kunovska, Magdalena Bogdanovska Todorovska, Boro Ilievski, Panche Zdravkovski, Selim Komina, Blagica Krstevska, Simonida Crvenkova, Marija Simonovska, Gordana Petrushevska, Sudheer Kumar Gara
pmc-12563640.description: Background/Objectives: Late diagnosis and inefficient treatment regimens lead to poor prognosis, with a low 5-year survival rate for both non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and small-cell lung cancer (SCLC). New targeted therapeutic agents can be developed and introduced only by first discovering new driver oncogenes and with a thorough investigation of the known driver genes.

pmc-12624129.title: A study of notation dependence in fraction magnitude processing using event related potentials
pmc-12624129.creator: Weimin Lin, Yun Pan, Jun Zhu, Liangzhi Jia, Huanyu Yang, Yajie Bi, Fangwen Yu, Di Zhang
pmc-12624129.description: Increasingly, research emphasizes that learning symbolic fractions (i.e., the quotient or ratio of two whole numbers) is challenging for both children and adults. However, humans and certain non-human animals are capable of representing the proportional relationships between non-symbolic magnitudes (e.g., dot arrays presented in different colors).

pmc-12651990.title: Comparative Analysis of Chromosome Repeat DNA Patterns in Four Amaranthus Species
pmc-12651990.creator: Alexandra V. Amosova, Olga Yu. Yurkevich, Alexey R. Semenov, Murat S. Gins, Julia V. Kalnyuk, Lyudmila V. Zemtsova, Alexander I. Morozov, Ekaterina D. Badaeva, Svyatoslav A. Zoshchuk, Olga V. Muravenko
pmc-12651990.description: Amaranthus L. includes valuable and promising crops of multi-purpose use, having high morphological diversity and complicated taxonomy. Their karyotypes and genomic relationships remain insufficiently studied. For the first time, a comparative repeatome analysis of Amaranthus tricolor L., Amaranthus cruentus L., and Amaranthus hypochondriacus L. was performed based on the high-throughput sequencing data obtained via bioinformatic analyses using the RepeatExplorer2/TAREAN/DANTE_LTR pipelines.

pmc-12721107.title: Prophylactic Use of Lipid Emulsion Therapy After Inadvertent Administration of 0.5% Ropivacaine for a Bier Block: A Case Report
pmc-12721107.creator: Alexander Luong, Sirimas Lau, Elizabeth Johnson-Gray, Rayyan Bhutta, Austin Shaffer, Mitchell Hughes, Andrew Gable, Matthias Franzen, Alparslan Apan
pmc-12721107.description: The Bier block for intravenous regional anesthesia is generally well tolerated, and few complications have been reported. It provides a bloodless surgical field and adequate analgesia when performed correctly. A diluted short‐acting local anesthetic such as 0.5% lidocaine is typically used. Our case is a 41‐year‐old female who presented for endoscopic carpal tunnel release of her right wrist.

pmc-13318847.title: New horizons in advance care planning: narratives, identity and cultural humility
pmc-13318847.creator: Sarah A Hopkins, Louisa Polak, Sarah E Hoare, Simon N Etkind, Luke Stalley, Roberta Lovick, Isla Kuhn, Rhian Simpson, Rowan H Harwood, Stephen Barclay, Michael Kelly
pmc-13318847.description: Advance care planning (ACP) is considered important for patient-centred care in serious illness, yet evidence it benefits patients is inconsistent. This reflects a lack of clarity over how ACP interventions are supposed to achieve their intended goals and what these goals should be, leading to variation in implementation.

pmc-13361858.title: Cross-Cultural Adaptation and Validation of the Turkish Form of the Awareness Scale on Consumption of Irradiated Foods (ASCIF)
pmc-13361858.creator: Demet Önen, Tiago Rusin, Wilma Maria Coelho Araújo
pmc-13361858.description: Food irradiation is a well-established technology endorsed by the World Health Organization (WHO) to enhance food safety. However, consumer awareness of irradiated foods remains remarkably low across diverse cultural contexts. This study aimed to cross-culturally adapt and validate the Turkish form of the Awareness Scale for Consumption of Irradiated Foods (ASCIF).

pmc-13366972.title: Association between corneal edema and corneal astigmatism after Descemet membrane endothelial keratoplasty
pmc-13366972.creator: Chung Young Kim, Mee Kum Kim
pmc-13366972.description: PurposeTo evaluate changes in corneal astigmatism after DMEK and determine the predictive value of preoperative central corneal thickness (CCT) for postoperative astigmatic change.MethodsFifty-five eyes with Fuchs’ endothelial dystrophy (FED) or pseudophakic bullous keratopathy (PBK) undergoing DMEK were analyzed. Auto kerato-refractometer (ARKRT)-derived anterior corneal astigmatic change was defined as the primary outcome in 55 eyes.

uslaw-cfr-t28-s570-44.title: 28 C.F.R. § 570.44 — Supervision and restraint requirements.
uslaw-cfr-t28-s570-44.creator: Bureau Of Prisons, Department Of Justice
uslaw-cfr-t28-s570-44.description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 28 (Judicial Administration), Part 570 (Community Programs). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Inmates under escort will be within the constant and immediate visual supervision of escorting staff at all times. Restraints may be applied to an inmate going on an escorted trip, after considering the purpose of the escorted trip and the degree of supervision.

uslaw-usc-t10-s666.title: 10 U.S.C. § 666 — Reserve officers not on the active-duty list
uslaw-usc-t10-s666.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s666.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part II (Personnel); Chapter 38 (Joint Officer Management). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Secretary of Defense shall establish personnel policies emphasizing education and experience in joint matters for reserve officers not on the active-duty list. Such policies shall, to the extent practicable for the reserve components, be similar to the policies provided by this.

uslaw-usc-t39-s1008.title: 39 U.S.C. § 1008 — Temporary employees or carriers
uslaw-usc-t39-s1008.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t39-s1008.description: United States Code, Title 39 (Postal Service); Part II (Personnel); Chapter 10 (Employment Within The Postal Service). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) A person temporarily employed to deliver mail is deemed an employee of the Postal Service and is subject to the provisions of chapter 83 of title 18 to the same extent as other employees of the Postal Service. (b).
